extra.message: Path traversal in document upload via unsanitized filename — An attacker could write files to arbitrary directories on the server's filesystem, potentially overwriting configuration files, gaining code execution, or reading sensitive files if the application later reads those files. [verified: No sanitization of the uploaded file name is performed before passing it to the FileField at line 108; Django's default storage does not prevent path traversal sequences. An authenticated client can thus write files to arbitrary directories, potentially overwriting sensitive files.]

Eval Injection RCE — Remote code execution on the server, allowing full system compromise. [verified: The `expr` GET parameter is passed to `eval()` with a restricted globals dict that removes `__builtins__`, but standard sandbox escape techniques (e.g., via `().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()`) can bypass this and achieve arbitrary code execution. The only upstream check is `_wrk_gate()`, which only ensures the user is a firm worker, not that the expression is safe.]

CSV Formula Injection in Audit Log Export — An attacker who controls audit log entry fields (e.g., description) can inject spreadsheet formulas into the exported CSV. When a firm administrator opens the file in a spreadsheet application (e.g., Microsoft Excel), formulas may execute, leading to arbitrary code execution or sensitive data exfiltration. [verified: The audit_log_export view writes raw user-supplied description fields (via log_event) to CSV without sanitizing formula prefixes like '=', '+', '-', '@'. No upstream validation or escaping is visible in the provided code, so an attacker can inject malicious spreadsheet formulas.]

Sensitive Data Exposure in Logs — Exposure of authentication tokens or other sensitive data in log files, enabling lateral movement or account compromise if logs are accessed by an attacker. [verified: In case_wire_tally_212, the Authorization header value is directly logged at line 80 without sanitization, exposing bearer tokens to log files. No compensating control such as redaction or masking is present upstream.]

Open redirect in notification read endpoint — An attacker can redirect an authenticated user to an arbitrary external URL after they perform a notification read action, enabling phishing attacks or other social engineering. [verified: The `redirect(request.POST.get('next') ... )` on line 79 uses an unvalidated attacker-controlled `next` parameter from POST data. No host allowlist, CSRF protection does not prevent same-site forged requests, and the parameter is reachable by any authenticated user.]
